articles.summary: SpruceID submitted comments to CMS on implementing new Medicaid community engagement requirements. Our recommendations focus on maximizing ex parte verification, expanding reliable evidence options, and keeping digital pathways voluntary, interoperable, and privacy-preserving.
articles.title: Recommendations to CMS on Medicaid Verification

articles.summary: Digital identity is becoming core policy infrastructure. Across benefits, financial regulation, privacy, and elections, better verification can strengthen trust while reducing unnecessary data collection and giving people greater control over their information.
articles.title: Digital Identity Is Becoming Policy Infrastructure

articles.summary: State-Endorsed Digital Identity (SEDI) is a rights-first approach to trusted digital identity, pioneered in Utah and gaining interest across states. In this post, we explain what SEDI is, the rights at its center, and our interpretation of how an endorsement framework can work in practice.
articles.title: What Is State-Endorsed Digital Identity (SEDI)?

articles.summary: As AI agents take on more consequential actions, they need a way to prove who authorized them and what they’re allowed to do. In this post, we explore an identity model that preserves accountability without creating a new surveillance layer.
articles.title: Who Sent This Agent? The Missing Identity Layer for AI Agents

articles.summary: Identity proofing establishes that a person is who they claim to be. For government services, the level of assurance required depends on the risk, and getting that calibration right shapes every downstream decision.
articles.title: What Is Identity Proofing? A Guide for Government IT Leaders

articles.summary: As states implement HR1, Medicaid and SNAP can share verification infrastructure without sharing eligibility rules, reducing duplicate verification while preserving privacy and user control.
articles.title: Medicaid and SNAP Need Different Rules, Not Separate Verification Infrastructure

articles.summary: Medicaid’s new community engagement requirements expose a broader challenge for digital government: how to verify facts across fragmented systems. A better model combines data-first verification with portable, privacy-preserving, standards-based digital evidence.
articles.title: Medicaid Work Requirements Are a Verification Infrastructure Challenge

articles.summary: SEDI's Digital Identity Bill of Rights creates obligations that policy language alone cannot enforce. Each right implies architectural constraints on verification, credential formats, wallet ecosystems, and governance.
articles.title: From Rights to Architecture: How SEDI Turns Digital Identity Principles Into Technical Requirements

articles.summary: States face three architectural models for HR1 verification, each with different implications for scalability, privacy, and vendor lock-in. The question is which model becomes the default for which type of evidence.
articles.title: Build, Integrate, or Reuse? An Architecture for HR1 Verification
